subject: SpinWave dedicated footprint: memory budgeting & precision impact
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver@spinwave.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@spinwave.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — 96k context, model footprint, and quant tradeoffs

Markus / Vanessa,

Thanks for taking a look. We're working through dedicated capacity sizing for an upcoming POC and need a clear recommendation on GPU footprint given the model and context window below. High level: we expect production to start with lower concurrency (2–4) then scale to 8 concurrent streams in steady state. Target p50 latency: <=200ms on generation steps.

Details:
- Model: customer-selected "L3-70b-chat" variant (70B-ish parameter family).
- Context window: planning up to 96k tokens for retrieval-augmented generations (cold start means the full prefix often present).
- Typical request size: 6k prompt tokens + ~512 generation tokens on average.
- Expected QPS: 12 requests/min initially, target committed concurrency 8 by month 3.
- Security: dedicated pool required, no cross-tenant sharing.

Questions we need answered for SOW and procurement:
1) Baseline GPU count for FP16 serving with full KV in GPU memory.
2) Savings if we move to INT8 or 4-bit quantized weights (and any implications on inference correctness/throughput).
3) Effect of KV offload to host memory (NVMe/host RAM) on latency and how many extra GPUs to provision to keep SLOs.
4) Any recommended hedging plan (buffer pod headroom) for bursts and model-version rollouts.

I'm attaching a very rough spreadsheet with our token distribution and expected concurrency. Oliver

Attachments: spinwave_kv_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@spinwave.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — 96k context, model footprint, and quant tradeoffs

Oliver — thanks, this is exactly the kind of detail we need. I'm looping in Vanessa (solutions) and Priyom (capacity planning) to put concrete numbers against the scenarios below. Quick take:

- FP16 (baseline weights in GPU memory) will be the safest route for the POC; expect higher GPU counts because model weights + large KV cache both need GPU addresses.
- Quantization (INT8/4-bit) can meaningfully drop the weight memory so you trade memory headroom for slightly more compute/packing overhead and potential minor regressions in some sensitive prompts. We should surface a small eval set as part of the SOW if you go below INT8.
- Offloading KV to host memory reduces GPU memory pressure but introduces extra latency and variability; still useful as a cost lever if you can accept a slightly higher p95.

Vanessa / Priyom — can you draft a 3-scenario table (FP16 baseline / INT8 / 4-bit + KV offload) with per-GPU headroom, recommended reserved GPU count for committed pool, and notes on expected p50/p95 impacts? Aim to get this by EOD so SpinWave procurement can move the SOW along.

— Markus

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@spinwave.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — 96k context, model footprint, and quant tradeoffs

Oliver / team,

Attached is a scenario spreadsheet (spinwave_kv_estimate.xlsx) and a short allocator note (attached PDF). Below is a concise breakdown and recommendation. I kept the math explicit so your procurement/infra folks can validate.

Assumptions and method:
- Model weight sizing: approximate param*2 bytes for FP16. For the L3-70B family, FP16 weights ~= 140 GB. INT8 compressed+metadata ~= 40–55 GB (format dependent). 4-bit pack (with dequant on the fly) ~= 20–28 GB.
- KV cache per token (approx): KV_bytes_per_token = num_heads * head_dim * 2 (k+v) * bytes_per_elem. Using representative architecture (128 heads, head_dim=64, bytes_per_elem=2 for FP16) gives ~32 KB/token. That means a full 96k context -> ~3.1 GB of KV in FP16. (If internal architecture varies we should recalc, but formula holds.)
- Runtime memory: activation scratch, optimizer is minimal (inference-only), plus CUDA fragmentation; assume +10–15% overhead buffer.

Scenario table (summary):
1) FP16 weights, KV in GPU RAM (no offload)
   - Per-GPU memory required (single replica serving one stream): ~143 GB (weights 140 GB + KV slice for typical active window + buffer).
   - Realistic mapping: requires 2x 80GB GPUs pinned per replica (weight sharded) — but to keep latency SLOs and avoid cross-GPU KV RPC we recommend A100/80GB pods in multi-GPU configuration.
   - Committed pool (to support concurrency=8 with headroom and canaries): recommend 10 x A100 80GB equivalent (this accounts for model sharding and 20% headroom).
2) INT8 weights, KV in GPU RAM
   - Per-GPU memory required: weights drop to ~50 GB equivalent, KV unchanged for FP16 KV storage unless KV is quantized (see note).
   - Recommended reserved pool: 6 x A100 80GB equivalent (same sharding approach) — INT8 reduces GPU count by ~35–40%.
   - Notes: latency slightly better for memory-limited scenarios; validate output quality on your eval set.
3) 4-bit weights + KV offload to host (RAM / NVMe cache)
   - Per-GPU memory required: weights ~25 GB, KV sliced out to host reduces GPU DRAM needs but introduces an additional hop for KV fetches.
   - Recommended reserved pool: 4 x A100 80GB equivalent + NVMe-backed nodes for KV. Expect increase in p95 (typical +40–120ms depending on host interconnect and cache hit ratio).

Hedging and operational notes:
- Start the POC on INT8 with a 30-day evaluation: gives good cost/throughput while validating quality. Keep canary FP16 capacity in the pool (2 GPUs) so we can failover if a model regression is observed.
- For committed contracts: add 20% pod headroom above steady concurrency to handle bursts and rolling deploys.
- If you can accept KV quantization (store KV in INT8/4-bit for cold prefix), it reduces KV footprint further but requires validation for semantic fidelity.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with per-token math and a per-request example. Next: Priyom will produce the final per-GPU headcount recommendation tailored to your expected concurrency and SLO.

— Vanessa

Attachments: spinwave_kv_estimate.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_gpu_allocator_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Oliver Chen <oliver@spinwave.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@spinwave.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — 96k context, model footprint, and quant tradeoffs

Vanessa — this is helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifying questions before we run the eval: 

1) The KV_bytes_per_token calc looks high relative to what our embedder team expected. Can you confirm the head_count/head_dim you used? If SpinWave's model variant uses 64 heads and head_dim=128 instead that changes the per-token bytes — would you re-run the sheet with a few head-count/head-dim combos?

2) For the INT8 scenario, is there an expected CPU or GPU overhead for dequant at runtime that would push latency beyond our 200ms p50 target?

3) On the NVMe offload option: what are typical cache-hit ratios you see for RAG-style workloads (large prefix + short generated answer)? Any guidance on sizing host RAM vs NVMe warm cache?

We'll upload a 1000-example eval set and ask your team to run model-quality comparisons (vanilla FP16 baseline vs INT8) + perf runs. If INT8 passes quality we can move to the committed pool numbers you suggested.

— Oliver

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@spinwave.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — 96k context, model footprint, and quant tradeoffs

Oliver — quick update from capacity planning after re-running the sheet with options for 64/128 heads and realistic head_dim combos. I captured the outputs in the attached sheet and summarize the recommended committed pool below (rounding to whole GPUs and including 20% headroom):

- If model architecture uses 128 heads / head_dim=64 (our earlier calc) -> INT8 recommended pool: 6 GPUs (A10080 equiv); FP16 conservative pool: 10 GPUs.
- If model uses 64 heads / head_dim=128 -> per-token KV rises slightly; INT8 pool grows to 7 GPUs, FP16 to 11 GPUs.
- If you plan to actively use NVMe offload to lower monthly committed spend we recommend starting with INT8 + NVMe warm cache and 5 GPUs; expect to add 1–2 GPUs once production traffic patterns stabilizes to meet p95 constraints.

Operational checklist for SOW:
1) Include evaluation window (2 weeks) with baseline FP16 runs and INT8 runs on your supplied eval set.
2) Add clause for fallback capacity (we hold 2 FP16-capable GPUs reserved for an emergency rollback for first 90 days).
3) Define p50/p95 SLOs and an explicit KV quantization acceptance threshold.

I'll schedule a short call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet and finalize the SOW numbers.

— Priyom
